title: Removing three years weakened the monthly count test for deep M5.5+ earthquakes in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested monthly count variation for 787 ComCat earthquakes with preferred M at least 5.5 and depth at least 300 km in 2000-2025. The null fixes each annual total and assigns independent uniform event times within the year. The full Pearson score gave a one-sided Monte Carlo probability of 0.00122. Removing the three largest annual scores, with the same selection in every null draw, gave 0.04364. The removed years were 2018, 2010 and 2002. The trimmed score was 1.149 times its null mean. The outside-Fiji-Tonga trimmed check gave 0.06188. A secondary fixed-margin test allowed a common seasonal month pattern and gave 0.03740 after trimming. Three-year removal thus weakened the primary evidence, and a uniform claim across regions was not supported. This is a count-model check, not a discovery of deep aftershocks or proof of a physical cause. Mixed magnitude methods, a short retrospective catalog, boundary choices and unmodeled rate changes limit inference. Code, aggregate counts, random score arrays, source hashes, validation and a figure are included. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Annual monthly-count scores and trimmed observed-to-null ratios for ComCat deep earthquakes in 2000-2025. Each null draw uses its own three removed years.
